reference.title: Band Low Chest Press
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (the proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the data sheet was not read; the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you press forward and down, breathe in as the band draws the hands back to the chest.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s press, short hold, about 2 s back

prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen (bands are colour-coded by tension): pick one you can move for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve; step farther from the anchor, or choke up on the band, for more tension.
prescription.progression: More reps, a slower return, a step farther from the rack, then the next band up.

cues.text: Loop a band round each rack upright behind you, above shoulder height. Staggered stance, knees soft, ribs down; a band end in each hand beside the lower chest, palms down, elbows back and out about 45 degrees.
Breathe out and press forward and slightly down, about 15-20 degrees below horizontal, until the arms are nearly straight in front of the lower chest.
Hands about lower-chest height and close together; shoulders down, do not let the band pull the trunk back.
Breathe in and let the hands come back to the chest slowly along the same line.
Brief pause with the band still taut, then press again.

mistakes.mistake: Pressing straight ahead or up so the line of pull no longer matches the band
mistakes.fix: Aim the hands at a point a little below the chest; the band should run in line with the forearms.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back or arching the low back as the band tightens
mistakes.fix: Ribs down, glutes lightly braced, weight over the front foot; use a lighter band.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging at the end of the press
mistakes.fix: Reach forward but keep the shoulders down.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the band snap the hands back

kinematics.norm: Hands travel forward and a little down (about 15-20 degrees below horizontal), the line of a decline press, which favours the lower (sternal) fibres of the chest (clinical opinion; the bench-angle EMG study tested only flat-to-incline angles, Rodríguez-Ridao 2020).
About 90-110 degrees at the chest to nearly straight (clinical opinion)
About 45 degrees from the body at the chest (clinical opinion)
Elastic resistance can give muscle activity comparable to free weights at a matched effort (Andersen 2010).
Staggered stance, knees soft, so the band does not pull you backward (clinical opinion)
About 1 s press and 2 s return (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Band Low Chest Press, video (movement reference)

Rodríguez-Ridao, Antequera-Vique, Martín-Fuentes and Muyor 2020, effect of five bench inclinations on the electromyographic activity of the pectoralis major, anterior deltoid and triceps brachii during the bench press exercise (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(19):7339; PMC7579505)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjornlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

Saeterbakken, van den Tillaar and Fimland 2011, a comparison of muscle activity and 1-RM strength of three chest-press exercises with different stability requirements (J Sports Sci 29(5):533-538; PubMed 21225489)

cautions: Check the band for nicks or tears before every session and replace a worn band; a band that snaps can hit the face or eyes.
Anchor the band to something that cannot move or slip (a rack upright, a pull-up bar or under the feet) and make sure it is secure before loading it.
Band tension rises as it stretches, so the load is heaviest at the end of the pull or push; let it return under control rather than snapping back.
Shoulder pain: shorten the range at the chest (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: palms facing each other and the elbows a little more tucked.
regressions: Lighter band or step closer to the rack.
progressions: Stronger band or a step farther from the rack.
Slower 3 s return with a pause at the chest.
Dips (when the gear is available) or a decline press.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main pusher; pressing down and forward biases the lower (sternal) fibres (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.pec_l: Main pusher; pressing down and forward biases the lower (sternal) fibres (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Flexes the shoulder with the chest; less involved than in an incline press because the arms finish below shoulder height.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Flexes the shoulder with the chest; less involved than in an incline press because the arms finish below shoulder height.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbows to finish the press.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straightens the elbows to finish the press.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Carries the shoulder blades forward round the rib cage at the end of the press.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Carries the shoulder blades forward round the rib cage at the end of the press.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Stabiliser at the elbow and shoulder (Saeterbakken 2011 found higher biceps activity with less stable loads).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Stabiliser at the elbow and shoulder (Saeterbakken 2011 found higher biceps activity with less stable loads).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: centres the head of the upper arm (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Control the shoulder blades on the return.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Control the shoulder blades on the return.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk upright against the band (clinical opinion).
